analysis_scope: 78 air quality stations paired with 2024 township income medians

data_sources.pollution: AQX_P_15 verified hourly data, annual means computed from numeric hours
data_sources.income: 2024 township-level filing unit income medians from official FIA aggregates

key_findings: NO2 shows a positive correlation with township income median (r=0.32, rho=0.40), meaning higher-income townships tend to have higher NO2, contrary to a simple environmental injustice expectation
PM2.5 and SO2 show essentially no linear association with income
The NO2-income positive association persists after excluding Taipei and appears within several counties
Interpretation: NO2 is strongly traffic-related; urban density correlates with both income and NO2 in Taiwan context
limitations: Station-level concentrations are not personal exposure estimates
Only 78 of 368 townships have stations; geographic coverage is uneven
Numeric hours are not certified valid hours; official invalid flags not separately parsed
Three global missing dates (2024-06-23, 2024-08-31, 2024-09-01) carry no data and are not imputed
Income is filing-unit comprehensive income median, not household disposable income
Station township assignment uses current metadata; 2024 historical station status not independently verified
Some station-to-township assignments for 11 stations were manually mapped and should be verified against official station metadata
